newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end slightly up, eye on U.S. mkt.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end slightly up, eye on U.S. mkt.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly higher Wednesday after a slow session spent watching U.S. Treasuries as traders sought a clear direction for the market.
"The market was just watching the U.S. Treasury as in recent days," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 93 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.05 at 122.95.
"There was little activity in local bonds - everything depends on the markets abroad," added the trader.
And with U.S. Treasuries seemingly range-bound in the lack of any expected market-moving news this week, Argentine bonds were not seen making any sharp moves either.
"The flow are trendless," said another trader.
It may take until next week with the release of important U.S. economic indicators to get the market to stake out a clear direction, traders said.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.13 percent from 5.88 percent.
